title: Cyber Intelligence Platform
summary: End-to-end platform for collecting public web content, analyzing information risk signals with Spark, NLP, graph mining, and exposing alerts through FastAPI and Streamlit.

details.problem: Public information streams are massive, heterogeneous, and difficult to analyze manually. Analysts need a way to detect signals such as toxic content, political polarization, suspicious narratives, graph-based coordination, and abnormal publishing behavior across articles, sources, authors, and comments.
details.dataset: The platform collects articles from configurable news sources such as AP News, USA Today, NBC News, Breitbart, and Radio-Canada, plus YouTube metadata and comments by keyword. Raw documents are stored in MongoDB, then enriched into Spark collections for preprocessed articles, analyzed comments, graph nodes and edges, usage signals, temporal anomalies, intelligence scores, and final alerts.
details.approach:
Designed a modular cyber-intelligence architecture with MongoDB as the central persistence layer and Docker Compose for local orchestration. Scrapy spiders collect source-specific articles through JSON configurations, while an optional YouTube collector expands the corpus with video metadata and comments.

Implemented a five-stage Apache Spark pipeline:
1. Preprocess raw articles by cleaning HTML, normalizing text, detecting language, deduplicating content, extracting links, and identifying named entities.
2. Run web content mining with toxicity scoring, polarization analysis, sentiment analysis, zero-shot topic classification, suspicious narrative detection, and optional AI-generated text detection.
3. Build a heterogeneous graph connecting sources, articles, authors, named entities, citations, and co-occurrences, then compute centrality and relational risk scores.
4. Analyze usage patterns such as source activity, author activity, propagation speed, and temporal anomalies using statistical signals.
5. Fuse content, graph, and usage signals into final intelligence scores and severity-ranked alerts.

Exposed the enriched data through a FastAPI REST API and built an interactive Streamlit dashboard for KPIs, score distributions, graph exploration, anomalies, alerts, and MongoDB collection inspection.
details.results: The system produces actionable cyber-intelligence indicators across multiple analysis dimensions. The dashboard summarizes 451 scored articles, 3,939 generated alerts, 4 monitored sources, 5,000 authors, and 1,113 detected anomalies. It also provides explainable alert reasons, severity distributions, topic analysis, usage anomalies, and direct exploration of the MongoDB collections produced by the Spark pipeline.
details.limitations: The quality of the scores depends on the diversity and volume of collected content. Scrapy selectors require maintenance when websites change their HTML structure. Local NLP inference can be memory intensive without GPU resources, so the pipeline includes heuristic fallback modes. The generated risk scores are decision-support indicators and still require human interpretation to avoid false positives.

title: Real-Time Credit Fraud Detection Platform
summary: End-to-end Big Data platform for real-time credit card fraud detection using Kafka, Spark Structured Streaming, PostgreSQL, Airflow, Streamlit, and a hybrid ML-based scoring engine.

details.problem: Financial transactions must be monitored in real time to detect suspicious behavior before fraudulent activity causes financial loss. Traditional batch processing is too slow, while simple rule-based systems are often rigid and unable to adapt to complex fraud patterns.
details.dataset: Used the Credit Card Fraud Detection dataset with anonymized PCA features V1 to V28, Time, Amount, and Class. The dataset was replayed as a streaming source and enriched with simulated business fields such as user ID, country, usual country, merchant category, payment method, device ID, and IP address.
details.approach:
Built an end-to-end real-time fraud detection platform that ingests transaction streams through Apache Kafka, processes them with Spark Structured Streaming, applies a hybrid fraud detection engine combining rule-based scoring, behavior analysis, and Machine Learning probability, then stores results in PostgreSQL and visualizes fraud insights in a Streamlit dashboard. The platform also includes Apache Airflow workflows for reporting, data quality checks, alert repair, and model evaluation.

Implemented a complete real-time data pipeline:
1. A Python producer replays credit card transactions and sends JSON messages to Kafka.
2. Spark Structured Streaming consumes the transactions_raw topic.
3. Spark parses, cleans, and enriches each transaction.
4. A hybrid detection engine calculates rule-based score, behavior score, ML fraud probability, and final hybrid score.
5. Transactions are classified as NORMAL, SUSPICIOUS, or FRAUD.
6. Results are stored in PostgreSQL.
7. Streamlit displays real-time KPIs, fraud trends, alerts, and model evaluation.
8. Airflow generates reports, checks data quality, repairs missing alerts, and exports model evaluation metrics.
details.results:
The system successfully detects normal, suspicious, and fraudulent transactions in real time. The dashboard includes fraud KPIs, hybrid score distributions, ML probability analysis, alert tables, and a Model Evaluation section with precision, recall, F1-score, accuracy, true positives, false positives, true negatives, and false negatives.

Example observed evaluation:
- True positives: 168
- False positives: 38
- True negatives: 521
- False negatives: 0
- Precision: 81.55%
- Recall: 100%
- F1-score: 89.84%
- Accuracy: 94.77%
details.limitations: The dataset features are anonymized, so some business fields are simulated. The fraud replay ratio is adjusted for demonstration. The system is not connected to a real banking API, and production-grade authentication, monitoring, and model registry are future improvements.

title: Satellite Image Super-Resolution using Deep Learning
summary: Developed a 4x super-resolution system for satellite imagery using advanced GAN and CNN architectures.

details.problem: Low-resolution satellite imagery limits the accuracy of remote sensing applications such as urban planning and environmental monitoring.
details.dataset: Standard super-resolution benchmark datasets (Div2K, Flickr2K) adapted for satellite imagery.
details.approach: Implemented and compared multiple architectures (SRCNN, SRResNet, EDSR, ESRGAN). Proposed a novel multi-scale, frequency-separated model to enhance detail reconstruction.
details.results: Achieved competitive performance across PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS metrics, significantly improving visual quality of 4x upscaled images.
details.limitations: Inference time for GAN-based models remains a challenge for real-time applications on edge devices.

title: Automatic License Plate Recognition (LPR)
summary: Real-time interactive platform for detecting and recognizing vehicle license plates.

details.problem: Manual vehicle tracking is inefficient and prone to errors. Automated systems need to be robust to varying lighting and angles.
details.dataset: Custom dataset of vehicle images collected under various conditions, annotated for license plate detection.
details.approach: Built a pipeline using YOLO for object detection to locate plates and Tesseract OCR for character recognition. Integrated into an interactive platform for real-time video processing.
details.results: Successfully detected and recognized plates with high accuracy in real-time video streams, outputting annotated visual results.
details.limitations: OCR accuracy drops in low-light conditions or with dirty/obscured plates.

title: Rainfall Prediction — Rain in Australia
summary: Machine Learning pipeline to predict rainfall occurrence based on daily weather observations.

details.problem: Accurate rainfall prediction is crucial for agriculture and water resource management.
details.dataset: Rain in Australia dataset containing daily weather observations from numerous weather stations.
details.approach: Performed data cleaning and feature engineering. Trained and evaluated multiple models including Random Forest, SVM, Naive Bayes, and Logistic Regression.
details.results: Achieved 84% prediction accuracy with the optimized Random Forest model.
details.limitations: Model performance varies by region due to localized climate micro-patterns.
